We need to build an app. Tech choice: static HTML site (no package.json) means served by default-start. Could use CDN libs for PDF operations. Requirements: split PDF by range, compress PDF, and other useful PDF tools, glassy theme. Must work fully client-side likely (no backend). Use pdf-lib from CDN? Environment may have restricted egress in browser (network). Better to vendor libraries locally. We can npm install pdf-lib, pdfjs-dist, maybe download via npm and copy dist files. The server serves static assets with mime. If package.json exists with vite, it builds. Simpler: static index.html + local JS/CSS + vendored libs.

Need app with several tools:
- Split PDF (by range, extract pages, split each page, fixed chunks)
- Compress PDF (image-based downsampling / recompress). Pure client side compression is tricky. Could use pdf-lib to re-save with object streams or use pdf.js render pages to JPEG at chosen quality then rebuild PDF. That is actual compression (rasterization). Also offer lossless "optimize" (remove metadata, object streams). Could implement both modes: "Smart compress" rasterize pages at chosen DPI/quality.
- Merge PDFs, rotate pages, delete pages, extract images, PDF to images (JPG/PNG), images to PDF, watermark, page numbers, protect? Encryption isn't in pdf-lib. Sign? Add metadata? Reorder pages. We should build ~8-10 tools.

Need a polished glassy theme: gradient background with animated blobs, frosted glass panels, blur, highlight borders, vibrant accents. UX: sidebar with tool categories, main workspace, file dropzone, per-tool options, processing progress, download results. Fully responsive. Include demo PDF generation so user can try without a file. Use local PDF.js worker. Need to be careful with pdfjs-dist version and worker. We can vendor pdf.js legacy build or modern build. Browser Chromium supports modules. We'll use pdf-lib UMD (pdf-lib.min.js) and pdf.js UMD build.

Compression approach: render each page to canvas using pdf.js at chosen scale based on target DPI, encode JPEG, embed into new PDF via pdf-lib at original page dimensions. This reduces file dramatically for image heavy docs; for text PDFs it might increase. Show comparison and offer "keep smaller" - if output bigger, return original? Better show result and note. Implement presets: Balanced (110 DPI, 0.72), Strong (80 DPI, 0.6), Extreme (60 DPI, 0.45). Also maybe "Lossless" using pdf-lib save with useObjectStreams (not much). Fine.

Other tools:
1. Split PDF — modes: ranges/extract, every page, fixed chunks. Produce ZIP? Could produce multiple PDFs in ZIP via fflate. Vendor fflate. Or output as multiple download buttons. Simpler: multiple files with individual download, plus "download all (.zip)" with fflate. We can vendor fflate.
2. Merge PDFs.
3. Compress.
4. Delete pages.
5. Rotate pages.
6. Reorder/organize pages? Maybe heavy. Could implement visual page thumbnails and reorder via drag? Nice but time. A simpler "Page organizer" with thumbnails and drag/delete/rotate is impressive. But keep scope manageable.
7. Images to PDF.
8. PDF to images (ZIP download).
9. Watermark (text, opacity, rotation, color, position tile/single).
10. Page numbers (position, format).
11. Add metadata? Not that useful.
12. PDF to text? Extract text using pdf.js and download .txt — useful.
13. Protect PDF? Can't encrypt via pdf-lib. Skip.
14. Crop? Could do "resize/scale to A4" or "N-up" maybe.

We need a complete, polished product. Let's plan architecture:

Static site:
- index.html
- assets/styles.css
- assets/app.js (main module maybe ES module)
- vendor/pdf-lib.min.js (UMD -> window.PDFLib)
- vendor/pdf.min.js and pdf.worker.min.js (UMD pdfjs)
- vendor/fflate.min.js (window.fflate)
- favicon.svg maybe
- README update? User asked app, not necessarily docs, but we can update README with run instructions.

Need to source libraries. Check network. Use npm pack? Let's try npm install pdf-lib pdfjs-dist fflate in temp. Then copy. Could use CDN via webfetch and write file, but npm is better.

Let's inspect versions. We'll npm pack to /tmp/pdflibs or install project dependencies then copy dist. Simpler: `npm install --no-save pdf-lib@1.17.1 pdfjs-dist@4.x fflate` then copy from node_modules. But static site with node_modules shouldn't remain; remove node_modules after copying and no package.json, so default-start uses html type.

- Complete an Indonesian-language PDF tools web app with a glassy visual theme and useful browser-based PDF operations.
